offline_note: Offline: showing the built-in question bank. Company-style and AI questions need internet.

general.question: Tell me about yourself.
general.hint: Present, past, future in about 90 seconds, tied to this role.

general.question: Why do you want this role and this company?
general.hint: Two specific reasons about the work, not only salary.

general.question: What is your biggest strength and a weakness you are fixing?
general.hint: Real weakness plus concrete steps and progress.

general.question: Tell me about a time you failed.
general.hint: Own it, show the lesson and what you changed.

general.question: Describe a conflict with a colleague or manager.
general.hint: STAR, stay professional, focus on resolution.

general.question: How do you handle tight deadlines and many priorities?
general.hint: A method plus an example with the result.

general.question: Where do you see yourself in five years?
general.hint: Growth tied to the role, honest and realistic.

QA Automation Engineer.question: What is the difference between smoke, sanity and regression testing?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Define each in one line, then say when you run it in your pipeline.

QA Automation Engineer.question: How do you decide which test cases to automate?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Repeatable, stable, high-risk, data-heavy flows first. Mention ROI and maintenance cost.

QA Automation Engineer.question: How do you handle flaky tests in Selenium or Playwright?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Explicit waits, stable locators, test isolation, retries only as a last step, quarantine and root-cause.

QA Automation Engineer.question: Explain the Page Object Model and why you use it.
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Separate locators and actions from tests. Give one real example and the maintenance benefit.

QA Automation Engineer.question: How do you test REST APIs? What do you assert besides status code?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Schema, headers, response time, negative cases, auth, idempotency. Name your tool (Postman, RestAssured).

QA Automation Engineer.question: Design an automation framework from scratch for a new web product.
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Language and tool choice, structure, reporting, CI, test data, parallel runs, how you would scale it.

QA Automation Engineer.question: How do you run automation in CI/CD and decide when a build is blocked?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Quality gates, test levels per stage, flaky policy, reports, who gets notified.

QA Automation Engineer.question: Tell me about a critical bug you found late. What did you change after?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: STAR format. End with a process change, not just the fix.

QA Automation Engineer.question: Developers say your failing test is a test problem, not a bug. What do you do?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Reproduce, share evidence, pair on it, stay factual and calm.

QA Automation Engineer.question: The release is tomorrow and 15% of regression is failing. What is your call?
QA Automation Engineer.hint: Triage by risk, separate real bugs from flakiness, give a clear go/no-go with data.

Java Developer.question: What is the difference between an interface and an abstract class in Java?
Java Developer.hint: Multiple inheritance of type, default methods, state. Give when you pick each.

Java Developer.question: Explain the difference between == and equals(), and why hashCode matters.
Java Developer.hint: Reference vs value equality, the contract, HashMap behavior.

Java Developer.question: How does HashMap work internally? What changed in Java 8?
Java Developer.hint: Buckets, hashing, collisions, treeification, resize, thread-safety.

Java Developer.question: Explain how Spring Boot auto-configuration and dependency injection work.
Java Developer.hint: Component scan, conditional beans, starters, constructor injection.

Java Developer.question: What are the differences between synchronized, volatile and ReentrantLock?
Java Developer.hint: Visibility vs atomicity, fairness, when each is enough.

Java Developer.question: How would you find and fix a memory leak in a production Java service?
Java Developer.hint: Heap dump, GC logs, profilers, typical causes (static maps, listeners, thread locals).

Java Developer.question: Design a REST service that handles 5,000 requests per second.
Java Developer.hint: Stateless design, caching, DB pooling, async, rate limits, observability.

Java Developer.question: Describe a time you improved the performance of an application.
Java Developer.hint: Measure before and after with numbers.

Java Developer.question: A production API is returning 500 errors after a deployment. Walk me through your first 15 minutes.
Java Developer.hint: Check rollback option, logs, metrics, recent change, communicate status.

Java Developer.question: A client wants a feature that will hurt system design. How do you respond?
Java Developer.hint: Understand the real need, present trade-offs, offer an alternative, document the decision.

Python Developer.question: What is the difference between a list, tuple, set and dict?
Python Developer.hint: Mutability, ordering, lookup cost, a typical use for each.

Python Developer.question: Explain decorators and generators with a use case.
Python Developer.hint: Wrapping behavior, lazy iteration, a real example from your work.

Python Developer.question: What is the GIL and how does it affect concurrency?
Python Developer.hint: CPU-bound vs I/O-bound, threads vs processes vs asyncio.

Python Developer.question: How do you structure a FastAPI or Django project for a team?
Python Developer.hint: Layers, settings, dependency injection, tests, migrations.

Python Developer.question: How do you write testable Python code? What do you mock and what not?
Python Developer.hint: pytest, fixtures, mock external boundaries only.

Python Developer.question: A Python service uses too much memory. How do you diagnose it?
Python Developer.hint: tracemalloc, profilers, generators, chunking, leak patterns.

Python Developer.question: Design a background job system with retries and idempotency.
Python Developer.hint: Queue, workers, retry with backoff, dedupe keys, dead-letter handling.

Python Developer.question: Tell me about a bug that took you a long time to find.
Your script processes a 10 GB file and crashes. What do you change?
Python Developer.hint: Stream, chunk, avoid loading all in memory, checkpoint.

Python Developer.question: You inherit an untested legacy codebase and must add a feature in a week.
Python Developer.hint: Characterization tests around the change, small safe steps, communicate risk.

Business Analyst.question: What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements?
Business Analyst.hint: Give two examples of each from a real project.

Business Analyst.question: What artifacts do you create in a project, and when?
Business Analyst.hint: BRD, user stories, process flows, wireframes, traceability matrix.

Business Analyst.question: How do you write good user stories and acceptance criteria?
How do you prioritize requirements when everything is urgent?
Business Analyst.hint: MoSCoW, value vs effort, stakeholder alignment, trade-off conversation.

Business Analyst.question: How do you validate requirements with stakeholders?
Walk me through how you would map an as-is to to-be process for onboarding.
Business Analyst.hint: Interviews, current flow, pain points, gaps, target flow, KPIs.

Business Analyst.question: Tell me about a time stakeholders disagreed on requirements.
Business Analyst.hint: STAR. Focus on how you facilitated the decision.

Business Analyst.question: Scope creep is hitting the sprint. What do you do?
Business Analyst.hint: Impact analysis, change request, product owner decision, document it.

Business Analyst.question: A client changes a core requirement two days before UAT.
Business Analyst.hint: Assess impact, options with cost and date, get written approval.

Business Analyst.question: What SQL or data skills do you use as a BA?
Business Analyst.hint: Joins, filters, validating reports, finding data gaps.

Data Analyst.question: What is the difference between INNER, LEFT and FULL joins?
Data Analyst.hint: One-line definitions and which rows each keeps.

Data Analyst.question: How do you clean a messy dataset?
Data Analyst.hint: Missing values, duplicates, types, outliers, documenting every step.

Data Analyst.question: Write or explain a query for the second highest salary per department.
Data Analyst.hint: Window functions (DENSE_RANK) vs subquery; mention ties.

Data Analyst.question: How do you choose the right chart for a business question?
Data Analyst.hint: Match chart to question, avoid clutter, one key message.

Data Analyst.question: A KPI dropped 20% this week. How do you investigate?
Data Analyst.hint: Check data quality first, segment by dimension, time, release, external events.

Data Analyst.question: How would you design an A/B test and read the result?
Data Analyst.hint: Hypothesis, metric, sample size, duration, significance vs practical impact.

Data Analyst.question: Tell me about an analysis that changed a business decision.
Data Analyst.hint: STAR with the number that mattered.

Data Analyst.question: A manager asks for a dashboard by tomorrow with unclear requirements.
Data Analyst.hint: Ask 3 key questions, ship a small version, iterate.

Data Analyst.question: Two reports show different revenue numbers. What do you do?
Data Analyst.hint: Definitions, filters, sources, reconcile, document the single source of truth.

Data Analyst.question: Which tools have you used (Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Python) and for what?
Data Analyst.hint: Be specific about one project per tool.

DevOps Engineer.question: What is CI/CD and what does your pipeline look like?
DevOps Engineer.hint: Stages: build, test, scan, deploy, with a real tool example.

DevOps Engineer.question: Explain containers vs virtual machines.
DevOps Engineer.hint: Isolation level, startup, resource use, when each fits.

DevOps Engineer.question: How do you manage infrastructure as code with Terraform?
DevOps Engineer.hint: State, modules, environments, plan/apply review, drift.

DevOps Engineer.question: How do you do zero-downtime deployments in Kubernetes?
DevOps Engineer.hint: Rolling update, readiness probes, blue-green or canary, rollback.

DevOps Engineer.question: How do you monitor a production system?
DevOps Engineer.hint: Metrics, logs, traces, SLOs, useful alerts vs noise.

DevOps Engineer.question: A pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. Walk me through debugging.
DevOps Engineer.hint: describe, logs (previous), events, config, probes, resources.

DevOps Engineer.question: Design a secure CI/CD pipeline.
DevOps Engineer.hint: Secrets handling, least privilege, image scanning, signed artifacts, approvals.

DevOps Engineer.question: Tell me about an outage you handled.
Deployment frequency is low because releases are scary. What do you do?
DevOps Engineer.hint: Smaller changes, automated tests, feature flags, safe rollback.

DevOps Engineer.question: Cloud costs doubled this month. How do you find out why?
DevOps Engineer.hint: Cost explorer, tags, top services, idle resources, ownership.

Frontend Developer.question: Explain the difference between let, const and var, and hoisting.
What is the box model and how do flexbox and grid differ?
Frontend Developer.hint: One-dimensional vs two-dimensional layout with a use case each.

Frontend Developer.question: How does the React rendering cycle work? When do you use useMemo or useCallback?
Frontend Developer.hint: State change, reconciliation, avoid premature optimization, measure first.

Frontend Developer.question: How do you improve page load performance?
Frontend Developer.hint: Bundle size, lazy loading, images, caching, Core Web Vitals.

Frontend Developer.question: How do you make a web app accessible?
Frontend Developer.hint: Semantic HTML, keyboard, ARIA only when needed, contrast, screen reader testing.

Frontend Developer.question: Design the frontend of a real-time dashboard with large data.
Frontend Developer.hint: State management, virtualization, websockets, throttling, error states.

Frontend Developer.question: Tell me about a UI bug that was hard to reproduce.
The designer's mock cannot be built as drawn. What do you do?
Frontend Developer.hint: Explain constraint, offer closest option, agree quickly.

Frontend Developer.question: Users report the app is slow only on mobile. How do you investigate?
Frontend Developer.hint: Real-device profiling, network throttling, long tasks, images, JS cost.

Frontend Developer.question: How do you test frontend code?
Frontend Developer.hint: Unit, component, e2e, what you mock, one real example.

Project Manager.question: How do you plan a project and track progress?
Project Manager.hint: Scope, WBS, milestones, risks, a status cadence and tool.

Project Manager.question: Agile vs waterfall: when do you use which?
Project Manager.hint: Requirement stability, feedback needs, team and client context.

Project Manager.question: How do you manage risks?
Project Manager.hint: Risk register, probability and impact, owners, mitigation, reviews.

Project Manager.question: How do you handle a client who keeps changing scope?
Project Manager.hint: Change control, impact on time and cost, written approval.

Project Manager.question: Which metrics do you report to stakeholders?
Project Manager.hint: Velocity or burn-up, budget, risks, quality, blockers, forecast.

Project Manager.question: A project is 30% behind schedule. What are your options?
Project Manager.hint: Root cause, re-baseline, scope cut, resources, honest client conversation.

Project Manager.question: Tell me about a conflict in your team and how you resolved it.
Project Manager.hint: STAR with the outcome and what you learned.

Project Manager.question: Your key developer resigns mid-sprint.
Project Manager.hint: Knowledge transfer, re-plan, inform stakeholders, backfill.

Project Manager.question: Two senior stakeholders give you conflicting priorities.
Project Manager.hint: Bring them together, use business value, get one decision owner.

Project Manager.question: How do you manage offshore and onshore teams across time zones?
Project Manager.hint: Overlap hours, clear handoffs, written updates, ownership.

Data Engineer.question: What is the difference between ETL and ELT?
Data Engineer.hint: Where transformation happens and why modern warehouses favor ELT.

Data Engineer.question: What is partitioning and why does it matter?
Data Engineer.hint: Prune data scans, choose key by access pattern.

Data Engineer.question: How do you design an idempotent pipeline?
Data Engineer.hint: Deterministic keys, upserts, replay safely, checkpointing.

Data Engineer.question: Batch vs streaming: how do you choose?
Data Engineer.hint: Latency need, cost, complexity, a concrete example.

Data Engineer.question: How do you ensure data quality?
Data Engineer.hint: Tests, schema checks, freshness, anomaly alerts, ownership.

Data Engineer.question: A Spark job is slow. How do you tune it?
Data Engineer.hint: Skew, shuffles, partitions, broadcast joins, caching, file sizes.

Data Engineer.question: Design a pipeline that ingests 1 TB per day from many sources.
Data Engineer.hint: Ingestion, landing zone, schema evolution, orchestration, monitoring, cost.

Data Engineer.question: Tell me about a pipeline failure that impacted business users.
An upstream team changes a schema without notice.
Data Engineer.hint: Detect, contract tests, quarantine, talk to owner, versioning.

Data Engineer.question: The finance report is wrong and the CFO is waiting.
Data Engineer.hint: Triage the lineage, communicate early, fix and prevent.

.NET Developer.question: What is the difference between .NET Framework, .NET Core and modern .NET?
.NET Developer.hint: Cross-platform, performance, side-by-side versions, say which you use and why you migrated.

.NET Developer.question: Explain value types vs reference types and boxing in C#.
.NET Developer.hint: Stack vs heap in simple terms, boxing cost, a case where it hurt performance.

.NET Developer.question: How do async and await work, and what goes wrong with .Result or .Wait()?
.NET Developer.hint: State machine, no thread blocked, deadlock in sync contexts, ConfigureAwait.

.NET Developer.question: Explain dependency injection lifetimes: transient, scoped, singleton.
.NET Developer.hint: One example each, and the captive dependency bug.

.NET Developer.question: Entity Framework: how do you avoid N+1 queries and slow queries?
.NET Developer.hint: Include/projection, AsNoTracking, indexes, look at the generated SQL.

.NET Developer.question: Design a Web API for orders with auth, versioning and high load.
.NET Developer.hint: JWT or OAuth, versioning, pagination, caching, rate limits, health checks, logging.

.NET Developer.question: How do you find a memory or CPU problem in a production ASP.NET service?
.NET Developer.hint: Counters, dotnet-dump or profiler, GC behavior, common leaks like event handlers.

.NET Developer.question: A client wants to move a legacy .NET Framework app to the cloud. How do you plan it?
.NET Developer.hint: Assess, strangler approach, upgrade path, tests first, containers or App Service, risks.

Full Stack Developer.question: Walk me through what happens from typing a URL to seeing the page.
Full Stack Developer.hint: DNS, TCP/TLS, request, server, response, render. Show you know both sides.

Full Stack Developer.question: REST vs GraphQL: when do you pick each?
Full Stack Developer.hint: Over-fetching, caching, tooling, team skills, a real example.

Full Stack Developer.question: How do you handle authentication and sessions in a SPA with an API?
Full Stack Developer.hint: Token vs cookie, httpOnly, refresh, CSRF and XSS tradeoffs.

Full Stack Developer.question: How do you design a database schema and API for a new feature?
Full Stack Developer.hint: Entities, relations, indexes, migrations, versioning, validation.

Full Stack Developer.question: How do you keep a React or Angular app fast?
Full Stack Developer.hint: Code splitting, memoization, lazy loading, bundle size, measuring with Lighthouse.

Full Stack Developer.question: Design a real-time notifications feature end to end.
Full Stack Developer.hint: WebSockets or SSE, queue, persistence, scale-out, retries, offline users.

Full Stack Developer.question: Tell me about a feature you shipped across front end and back end.
Full Stack Developer.hint: STAR. Show you owned the whole slice and measured the result.

Full Stack Developer.question: The page is slow in production but fast locally. How do you debug it?
Full Stack Developer.hint: Network tab, API timings, DB queries, payload size, caching, CDN, then fix the biggest cost.

Salesforce Developer.question: What is the difference between a workflow, Process Builder and Flow, and what do you use now?
Salesforce Developer.hint: Flow is the current tool, say when Apex is still better.

Salesforce Developer.question: Explain governor limits and name the ones you hit most.
Salesforce Developer.hint: SOQL queries, DML, CPU time, heap. Bulkify and avoid queries in loops.

Salesforce Developer.question: How do you write a bulk-safe Apex trigger?
Salesforce Developer.hint: One trigger per object, handler class, collections, maps, no SOQL or DML in loops.

Salesforce Developer.question: Lightning Web Components vs Aura: how do they communicate?
Salesforce Developer.hint: Properties, events, LMS, wire service, Apex calls. Say you prefer LWC.

Salesforce Developer.question: Explain the Salesforce security model.
Salesforce Developer.hint: Org-wide defaults, roles, profiles and permission sets, sharing rules, field-level security.

Salesforce Developer.question: How would you integrate Salesforce with an external ERP?
Salesforce Developer.hint: REST or platform events, named credentials, async Apex, retries, error logging, idempotency.

Salesforce Developer.question: How do you deploy and test changes across sandboxes?
Salesforce Developer.hint: SFDX or DevOps Center, Git, CI, test classes with 75% coverage but meaningful asserts.

Salesforce Developer.question: A nightly batch job fails halfway with record lock errors. What do you do?
Salesforce Developer.hint: Logs, batch size, ordering, retries, lock causes, make it re-runnable.

ServiceNow Developer.question: What are the core ServiceNow tables and how does the CMDB fit in?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: Task, incident, change, CI tables, relationships, keeping CMDB data trusted.

ServiceNow Developer.question: Business rule vs client script vs UI policy vs flow: when do you use each?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: Server vs client, timing (before, after, async), prefer no-code Flow when possible.

ServiceNow Developer.question: How do you build a catalog item with approvals and fulfillment?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: Variables, variable sets, workflow or Flow Designer, approvals, tasks, testing.

ServiceNow Developer.question: How do you integrate ServiceNow with another system?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: REST messages, Integration Hub, MID server, import sets, transform maps, error handling.

ServiceNow Developer.question: How do ACLs work and how do you debug one?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: Table, field, role, condition, script; security debugger.

ServiceNow Developer.question: How do you move and control changes between instances?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: Update sets vs app repository and source control, scoped apps, testing, back-out plan.

ServiceNow Developer.question: A form is slow to load. How do you find out why?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: Transaction logs, client scripts, business rules, onLoad scripts, related lists.

ServiceNow Developer.question: The business asks for heavy customization. How do you respond?
ServiceNow Developer.hint: Out-of-the-box first, upgrade cost, configuration over code, document the decision.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: Explain IAM users, roles and policies, and least privilege.
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: Roles over keys, scoped policies, MFA, one real example.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: What is the difference between EC2, ECS, EKS and Lambda?
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: Control vs convenience, cost model, when each fits.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: How do you design a VPC with public and private subnets?
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: CIDR plan, NAT, route tables, security groups vs NACLs, endpoints.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: How do you build highly available and fault tolerant systems on AWS?
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: Multi-AZ, auto scaling, load balancer, health checks, backups, RTO and RPO.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: How do you manage infrastructure as code?
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: Terraform or CloudFormation, state, modules, review and CI, drift detection.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: Your AWS bill doubled this month. What do you do?
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: Cost Explorer, tags, find top services, rightsizing, savings plans, guardrails and alerts.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: Design a secure multi-account setup for an enterprise.
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: Organizations, SCPs, landing zone, central logging, network hub, break-glass access.

AWS Cloud Engineer.question: An S3 bucket was found public. What are your first steps?
AWS Cloud Engineer.hint: Block access, assess exposure with logs, rotate secrets, report, add preventive controls.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: Explain the CIA triad and give a real example of each.
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Confidentiality, integrity, availability with simple incidents.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: What is the difference between a vulnerability, a threat and a risk?
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Define and link them: risk = likelihood x impact.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: Walk me through how you would triage a phishing alert.
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Headers, URLs, sandbox, affected users, block, reset, report, lessons.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: What is the MITRE ATT&CK framework and how do you use it?
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Map detections to tactics, find gaps, threat hunting.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: How do you use a SIEM such as Splunk or Sentinel day to day?
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Correlation rules, tuning false positives, dashboards, investigations.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: Describe the incident response lifecycle with a real or example incident.
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Prepare, detect, contain, eradicate, recover, lessons learned. Stay calm and structured.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: How do you prioritize 5,000 vulnerabilities from a scan?
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Exploitability, asset criticality, exposure, compensating controls, SLAs.

Cybersecurity Analyst.question: You see data leaving the network at 3 AM to an unknown IP. What now?
Cybersecurity Analyst.hint: Confirm, isolate host, preserve evidence, escalate, scope the damage, communicate.

Scrum Master.question: What are the Scrum events, roles and artifacts?
Scrum Master.hint: Name them briefly and the purpose of each.

Scrum Master.question: How do you run a retrospective that produces real change?
Scrum Master.hint: Format variety, one or two actions with owners, follow up next sprint.

Scrum Master.question: The team keeps missing sprint goals. What do you look at?
Scrum Master.hint: Estimation, interruptions, dependencies, WIP, data from velocity and burndown.

Scrum Master.question: How do you coach a Product Owner who changes priorities mid-sprint?
Scrum Master.hint: Protect the sprint, explain cost of change, backlog refinement, agree a rule.

Scrum Master.question: How do you scale Agile across several teams and dependencies?
Scrum Master.hint: Scrum of Scrums, SAFe or LeSS basics, program increments, shared board, risk.

Scrum Master.question: Tell me about a conflict in a team and how you handled it.
Scrum Master.hint: STAR. A servant leader facilitates, does not dictate.

Scrum Master.question: Management wants the team to commit to more than it can deliver.
Scrum Master.hint: Use data, show trade-offs, protect the team, offer options.

Scrum Master.question: A distributed team across US and India time zones loses focus. What do you change?
Scrum Master.hint: Overlap hours, async updates, clear working agreements, rotate meeting times.

Network Engineer.hint: Layers 1 to 7 with real examples: switch L2, router L3, TCP L4.

Network Engineer.question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP, and when do you use each?
Network Engineer.hint: Reliability vs speed, examples like web vs voice.

Network Engineer.question: How do OSPF and BGP differ, and where do you use each?
Network Engineer.hint: IGP vs EGP, metrics, convergence, typical designs.

Network Engineer.question: Explain VLANs, trunking and spanning tree.
Network Engineer.hint: Segmentation, tagging, loop prevention, a troubleshooting story.

Network Engineer.question: How do you troubleshoot a site that cannot reach the internet?

Network Engineer.question: Design a network for two offices and a data center with redundancy.
Network Engineer.hint: Dual links, SD-WAN or MPLS, VPN, HSRP or VRRP, segmentation, monitoring.

Network Engineer.question: How do firewalls, NAT and VPNs fit in a secure design?
Network Engineer.hint: Zones, policies, site-to-site and remote access, logging.

Network Engineer.question: A core switch fails at 2 PM on a business day.
Network Engineer.hint: Fail over, communicate, restore, root cause, post-incident review.

Machine Learning Engineer.question: What is overfitting and how do you prevent it?

Machine Learning Engineer.question: How do you choose evaluation metrics for an imbalanced classification problem?
Machine Learning Engineer.hint: Precision, recall, F1, PR-AUC over accuracy, business cost of errors.

Machine Learning Engineer.question: How do you take a model from notebook to production?
Machine Learning Engineer.hint: Packaging, API, versioning, CI/CD, monitoring, rollback.

Machine Learning Engineer.question: How do you detect and handle data drift and model decay?

Machine Learning Engineer.question: How do you build an LLM or RAG application and keep answers reliable?
Machine Learning Engineer.hint: Chunking, embeddings, retrieval quality, prompts, evals, guardrails, cost and latency.

Machine Learning Engineer.hint: Candidate generation, ranking, features, latency budget, feedback loop, A/B tests.

Machine Learning Engineer.question: The model is accurate offline but the business sees no gain. What now?

Data Scientist.question: Explain bias vs variance.

Data Scientist.question: A stakeholder does not trust your model. How do you win them over?

SAP Consultant.question: Walk me through a procure-to-pay or order-to-cash flow in SAP.

Sales / Business Development Executive.question: What is the difference between a lead, a prospect and a customer?
Sales / Business Development Executive.hint: Lead: possible interest. Prospect: qualified and fits. Customer: bought. Mention qualifying with budget, need and timeline.

Sales / Business Development Executive.question: How do you cold call or message a new lead?
Sales / Business Development Executive.hint: Research first, short opener, ask questions, give value, clear next step. Give a sample opening line.

Sales / Business Development Executive.question: A customer says 'your price is too high'. What do you say?
Sales / Business Development Executive.hint: Do not drop price first. Find the real concern, show value and ROI, compare fairly, offer options.

Sales / Business Development Executive.question: You are behind your monthly target with a week left. What do you do?
Sales / Business Development Executive.hint: Review pipeline, focus on hot leads, follow up, ask for support, stay ethical. Show a plan with numbers.

Sales / Business Development Executive.question: How do you handle rejection?
Sales / Business Development Executive.hint: Treat it as data, ask why, improve the pitch, keep your daily call count up.

Sales / Business Development Executive.question: Sell me this pen (or any product).
Sales / Business Development Executive.hint: Ask about their need first, then link features to benefits, handle one objection, close with a clear ask.

Sales / Business Development Executive.question: Tell me about a time you convinced someone to agree with you.
Sales / Business Development Executive.hint: STAR. Show listening first, then a clear result.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: What are the main channels of digital marketing?
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: SEO, SEM or paid ads, social media, email, content, affiliate. Say which you have actually worked on.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: What is the difference between SEO and SEM?
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: Organic vs paid search. Mention keywords, ranking time, cost.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: How do you do keyword research and on-page SEO?
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: Tools like Google Keyword Planner or Ubersuggest, intent, title, meta, headings, internal links, speed.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: How do you measure a campaign? Which metrics matter?
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: CTR, CPC, CPA, conversion rate, ROAS, bounce rate. Link metrics to the business goal.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: How would you run a Facebook or Instagram ad campaign for a small business?
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: Goal, audience, creative, budget, test variants, track with pixel, optimize weekly.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: What is Google Analytics and what do you check daily?
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: Traffic sources, user behavior, conversions, goals. Mention GA4.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: Your ads get clicks but no sales. What do you check?
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: Landing page, offer, audience, tracking, ad-to-page match, checkout friction. Fix one thing at a time.

Digital Marketing Executive.question: Tell me about a post or campaign you managed and its result.
Digital Marketing Executive.hint: Use real numbers even from a college or personal project: reach, leads, growth.

HR Executive.question: Why do you want a career in HR?
HR Executive.hint: People interest, helping both employees and company. Give a real reason, not 'I like people' only.

HR Executive.question: What are the main functions of HR?
HR Executive.hint: Recruitment, onboarding, payroll, attendance, employee relations, training, compliance.

HR Executive.question: Explain the recruitment process from requirement to joining.
HR Executive.hint: JD, sourcing, screening, interviews, offer, background check, onboarding. Mention drop-off handling.

HR Executive.question: How do you screen a resume and shortlist candidates?
HR Executive.hint: Must-have skills, experience fit, stability, communication, red flags. Check with the hiring manager.

HR Executive.question: What are PF, ESI, gratuity and the basics of a salary slip?
HR Executive.hint: Basic idea of each in simple words. Say you will always follow the company policy and labour law.

HR Executive.question: A selected candidate does not join on the date. What do you do?
HR Executive.hint: Call, find the reason, offer help, keep a backup candidate, learn for the future.

HR Executive.question: Two employees have a serious conflict. How do you handle it?
HR Executive.hint: Listen to both separately, stay neutral, find facts, follow policy, document, follow up.

HR Executive.question: Which HR tools or Excel skills do you use?
HR Executive.hint: ATS, Naukri or LinkedIn, Excel for trackers, basic formulas like VLOOKUP.

PHP Developer.question: What is the difference between echo and print, == and ===?
PHP Developer.hint: Short answers. Then say you use === for strict comparison.

PHP Developer.question: Explain GET vs POST and how sessions and cookies work in PHP.
PHP Developer.hint: Data in URL vs body, session on server, cookie on client, security basics.

PHP Developer.question: How do you prevent SQL injection and XSS in PHP?
PHP Developer.hint: Prepared statements with PDO, escape output, validate input, CSRF tokens.

PHP Developer.question: What is MVC and how does Laravel use it?
PHP Developer.hint: Model, View, Controller. Routes, Eloquent, Blade, migrations. Mention what you built.

PHP Developer.question: Explain joins in MySQL and how you make a query faster.
PHP Developer.hint: Inner and left join, indexes, EXPLAIN, avoid SELECT *.

PHP Developer.question: How do you build and secure a REST API in Laravel?
PHP Developer.hint: Resource controllers, validation, auth with Sanctum or JWT, status codes.

PHP Developer.question: A PHP page takes 8 seconds to load. How do you find the cause?
PHP Developer.hint: Profile queries, N+1, caching, opcache, image size, server logs.

PHP Developer.question: Tell me about a project you built in PHP.
PHP Developer.hint: Problem, your part, tools, one challenge, result. Offer a GitHub link.

Android Developer.question: Explain the Android activity lifecycle.
Android Developer.hint: onCreate, onStart, onResume, onPause, onStop, onDestroy. Say what you do in each.

Android Developer.question: What is the difference between an Activity and a Fragment?
Android Developer.hint: Screen vs reusable part of a screen, why fragments help on tablets and navigation.

Android Developer.question: Kotlin vs Java for Android: why Kotlin?
Android Developer.hint: Null safety, shorter code, coroutines, official preference.

Android Developer.question: How do you call an API and show data in a list?
Android Developer.hint: Retrofit, coroutines, ViewModel, LiveData or StateFlow, RecyclerView or Compose.

Android Developer.question: What is MVVM and why use it?
Android Developer.hint: Separate UI and logic, survives rotation, easier testing.

Android Developer.question: How do you store data locally?
Android Developer.hint: Room, SharedPreferences or DataStore, when to use each.

Android Developer.question: Your app crashes on some devices only. How do you debug?
Android Developer.hint: Crashlytics logs, reproduce on emulator, OS versions, memory, permissions, fix and test.

Android Developer.question: Tell me about an app you built or published.
Android Developer.hint: Purpose, features, tech, a hard problem solved. Share a Play Store or GitHub link.

UI/UX Designer.question: What is the difference between UI and UX?
UI/UX Designer.hint: UX is how it works and feels, UI is how it looks. Give a simple example.

UI/UX Designer.question: Walk me through your design process.
UI/UX Designer.hint: Research, personas, wireframes, prototype, test, iterate, hand-off.

UI/UX Designer.question: How do you do user research when you have no budget?
UI/UX Designer.hint: Talk to 5 users, surveys, competitor review, analytics, usability tests with friends.

UI/UX Designer.question: Which design tools do you use and how do you hand off to developers?
UI/UX Designer.hint: Figma, components, auto layout, design system, specs, comments, clear states.

UI/UX Designer.question: How do you make a design accessible?
UI/UX Designer.hint: Contrast, font size, touch targets, labels, keyboard use, do not rely on color alone.

UI/UX Designer.question: Redesign the checkout flow of a shopping app that has high drop-off.
UI/UX Designer.hint: Find where users drop, reduce steps, guest checkout, trust signals, test the change.

UI/UX Designer.question: A developer says your design is hard to build. What do you do?
UI/UX Designer.hint: Listen, understand the limit, find a simpler version, keep the user goal.

UI/UX Designer.question: Walk me through a project in your portfolio.
UI/UX Designer.hint: Problem, your role, process, final design, result. Be ready to explain every choice.

Banking Operations.question: What is KYC and why is it required?
Banking Operations.hint: Know Your Customer: identity and address proof, prevents fraud and money laundering, RBI rules.

Banking Operations.question: Explain the difference between savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
Banking Operations.hint: Purpose, interest, withdrawals, who uses each.

Banking Operations.question: What are NEFT, RTGS, IMPS and UPI?
Banking Operations.hint: Speed, limits and timing in simple words. Say UPI is instant and 24x7.

Banking Operations.question: How does a loan process work: from application to disbursal?
Banking Operations.hint: Application, documents, credit check, approval, sanction, agreement, disbursal.

Banking Operations.question: What is a CIBIL score and why does it matter?
Banking Operations.hint: Credit score range 300 to 900, affects loan approval and rate.

Banking Operations.question: A customer's transaction failed but money is debited. What do you do?
Banking Operations.hint: Check status, explain reversal timeline, raise a ticket, follow up, keep the customer informed.

Banking Operations.question: You notice a transaction that looks suspicious. What do you do?
Banking Operations.hint: Do not tip off the customer, follow the process, report to the compliance or AML team, document.

Banking Operations.question: How do you stay accurate with cash and numbers under pressure?
Banking Operations.hint: Double check, follow the checklist, reconcile daily, ask when unsure.

Accountant (Tally).question: What are the golden rules of accounting?
Accountant (Tally).hint: Personal, real and nominal accounts with the debit and credit rule for each, with one example.

Accountant (Tally).question: What is the difference between a voucher and a ledger in Tally?
Accountant (Tally).hint: Voucher records a transaction, ledger shows the account summary.

Accountant (Tally).question: How do you record a purchase with GST in Tally?
Accountant (Tally).hint: Create ledgers, purchase voucher, CGST and SGST or IGST, party details, check the entry.

Accountant (Tally).question: How do you do a bank reconciliation?
Accountant (Tally).hint: Match the bank statement with the books, list differences like cheques not cleared, prepare the BRS.

Accountant (Tally).question: What is GST and how do you file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B?
Accountant (Tally).hint: Output and input tax, return purpose and due dates, reconcile with books and 2B.

Accountant (Tally).question: What is TDS and where do you deduct it?
Accountant (Tally).hint: Tax deducted at source, common sections, rates, deposit and return, Form 16A.

Accountant (Tally).question: Your trial balance does not tally. How do you find the error?
Accountant (Tally).hint: Check totals, transposition errors, one-sided entries, suspense, review recent entries.

Accountant (Tally).question: Month-end is tomorrow and some invoices are missing. What do you do?
Accountant (Tally).hint: List the missing items, follow up now, book provisions if policy allows, tell your manager.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What do you know about the call centre industry?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: A call centre is a service desk where the customer associate handles a large volume of calls to provide services to the client.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What are the types of call centres? What is the difference?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Inbound: the associate receives calls about customers' queries or needs. Example: a customer calls a telecom company to ask about the current internet tariff. Outbound: the associate makes calls to customers for business or sales. Example: a bank calls to offer a personal loan.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is the difference between BPO and a call centre?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: A BPO (Business Process Outsourcing) organisation performs a process, or part of a process, for another business. Outsourcing is done to save cost or gain productivity. A call centre performs the part of a client's business that involves handling telephone calls, for example customer complaints. So a call centre can be considered a BPO.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is an international BPO?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: An international BPO serves customers outside India, for example in the US or UK. The work is often in night shifts because of their time zone. A call centre is one kind of BPO that handles customer calls. Tip: Say it in your own words. Mention that you are ready for shifts.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is a call centre job according to you?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: A call centre job means talking to customers, understanding their problem and helping them with the right solution. Tip: The interviewer is checking whether you know the job. Talk about helping customers with their problems.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What do you understand by "customer satisfaction"?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Any business depends on the quality of service offered to the customer. To do this, you need to understand the customer's needs and problems, think from their point of view and try to meet their demands. This is customer satisfaction.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What will you do if a customer abuses you on the phone?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: First, I will stay calm, listen to the customer's problem and try to understand what made them annoyed. Next, I will politely ask them to calm down. Then I will assure them that I will solve their problem. Last, I will find the root cause of the problem, fix it and make sure it does not happen again. Learning from the mistake can also improve the company's process and policy.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What qualities should a customer associate have to be a perfect customer associate?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Good listening skills, problem-solving, concentration and patience.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How do you handle work pressure?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: To handle a pressure situation, I keep my focus on work and avoid frustration. or "I have worked under pressure a lot during my college days. I have realised that I actually work well under pressure. The pressure brings out maximum efficiency in me."

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is your typing skill?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: My typing speed is around [your speed] words per minute with good accuracy. If you do not know your speed, say: I am good at typing and I practise regularly. Tip: Give your real number from a typing test. This is a quick-check question, so be honest.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Can you handle multiple calls at the same time?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: If you have experience, describe it. If you do not, say: once training is provided, I can handle multiple calls with ease. Tip: Never claim experience you do not have.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How do you rate yourself on communication skills?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I rate my communication skills around 8 out of 10. I am improving every day by speaking and listening in English. Tip: Call centres look for good communication, so rate yourself high but honestly, and mention how you improve.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is the key to success in a call centre?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: A call centre is all about providing quality service to the customer. If you handle customers well and offer good service, you can be successful in a call centre.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What procedure do you follow while talking to a customer?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: 1. Greet the customer. 2. Introduce yourself. 3. Ask how you can help. 4. Listen patiently. 5. Give the best possible solution. 6. Cross-check that the customer is satisfied. 7. Ask if they need any further help.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Do you like multi-tasking, or do you prefer to handle one problem at a time?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Depending on the situation, I can multi-task or handle one problem at a time. But multi-tasking has the upper hand because it increases efficiency in a call centre.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What if the customer is not happy with your answer or solution?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: If the customer is not happy with my answer or solution, I will ask them to hold the line and pass the call to a manager or team leader.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What will be your approach to improve customer service?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: For better customer service, I would take feedback from the customer and ask how we can improve in solving their problem and give them good service.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How do you deal with a difficult customer?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Listen actively. Rephrase their concerns. Give a workable solution. Take action and follow up. Fix the problem immediately. Use the feedback. Reduce unpleasant situations by doing proper research and preparation.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How do you measure good customer service?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Number of repeat customers. Number and type of complaints. Number of referrals from current customers. Sales figures, if the service is product based. Customer satisfaction surveys. Benchmarking against competitors. Rate of new customers enrolling. Number of returns.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What steps will you take to deal with an unsatisfied customer?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Apologise and offer a better option. Act quickly and resolve the complaint. Take responsibility for what made the customer unhappy. Compensate with a better deal or free service.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How can you resolve the problem to the customer's satisfaction?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Talk to the customer (a phone call is often quicker and more personal than a standard email or letter). Find out the problem and the requirement by listening carefully. Ask about wider issues with open questions, such as "Are you happy with our service or product?" Offer something back, such as an offer, discount or coupon, if there is a real issue and a chance of losing the customer. Confirm your solution with a follow-up email or letter to avoid disputes. Follow up regularly, and ask a team member to check that all is well.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is a back-end process?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Back office: the part of the company with employees doing administrative and support work. They do not deal directly with customers but are the backbone of the company. Example: in a bank or finance company, managing and settling accounts, clearing payments, updating records, running IT infrastructure, data entry and HR. The back office does not generate revenue, but the front-office sales team cannot complete a deal without its support. Front office: people who deal directly with customers, such as sales and customer support. They generate revenue. Back-office staff work behind the scenes, execute the deals sales brings in and take them to completion. Both offices must work hand in hand.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is the difference between a voice process and a non-voice process?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Hindi: Voice = call par baat. Non-voice = chat/email/typing. Apni pasand wajah ke saath.

BPO / Call Centre.question: The customer does not understand your English. What will you do?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Hindi: Dheere bolo, aasaan shabd, dohrao. Process allow kare to Hindi mein poochho.

BPO / Call Centre.question: You do not know the answer to a customer's question. What do you do?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Hindi: Andaza mat lagao. "Let me check" boliye, guide dekho ya team lead se poochho.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is AHT (average handling time) and why does it matter?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Hindi: Ek call par lagne wala average time. Speed ke saath sahi jawab bhi zaroori.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Tell me about a time you helped someone solve a problem.
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Hindi: Chhoti kahani: problem, aapne kya kiya, natija.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What salary do you expect?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Hindi: "Company ke fresher standard ke hisaab se, mujhe seekhna zyada zaroori hai."

BPO / Call Centre.question: Can you travel to the office daily?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Hindi: Doori aur time sach batao. Cab ho to bolo.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Can you stay focused on repetitive work?
Why did you leave your last job?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I am looking for better growth and more learning opportunities. I am thankful for what I learned at my last company. Tip: Never speak badly about a past employer. Talk about growth.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Tell us about your team mates and your team.
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I worked well with my team. When there were issues, I spoke openly with my team members and my team leader and focused on finishing the work properly. Tip: Stay positive. Do not complain about colleagues.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Why is there a gap in your work history?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I was feeling exhausted after years of non-stop work, so I decided to take a break and spend time with my family. I am happy to have returned fully recharged. Tip: Be honest, short and positive. Then say you are ready to work.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Can you tell us something about your previous boss?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: He was very friendly with me. He inspired me a lot. I have always tried to learn something new from him. Tip: Say something positive and what you learned.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What irritates you about co-workers?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I understand that teamwork is important. If someone is not serious about their work or does low-quality work that affects the whole project, I do not like it. But I try to talk to them politely and help. Tip: Pick a work habit, not a person, and end with how you handle it.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Is there any particular kind of person you cannot work with?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: No. I can work with all kinds of people. I focus on the work and respect everyone. Tip: Do not name types of people. Say you can work with everyone.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What qualities do you look for in your senior?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I look for qualities like intelligence, a good sense of humour and dedication to the team. Tip: Pick 2-3 positive qualities, like guidance, fairness and support.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What are the most important things for you as a manager?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Two things are most important for a manager to succeed: my team should be happy and keep performing, and the project I am working on with my team should finish successfully with minimum problems. Tip: Say team first, then results.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Tell me about yourself.
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: My name is [your name]. I am from [your city]. I have completed my [10th / 12th / graduation] in [your stream]. I learn quickly and I am a good listener. I want to start my career in [this role] and grow with your company. Tip: Use 4-5 short sentences: name, city, studies, one skill, why you want this job. Speak slowly and clearly. Hindi: Naam, shehar, padhai, ek skill aur is job ki wajah bataiye. Dheere aur saaf boliye.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What are your strengths?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: My greatest strength is my ability to learn things quickly. or "I think my greatest strength is my positive attitude, even in the hardest times."

BPO / Call Centre.question: What are your weaknesses?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I care too much about my work. or "I feel restless until my work is done."

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is your short-term goal?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: My short-term goal is to fulfil my parents' dreams.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is your long-term
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: My long-term goal is to become a respectable and successful person.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Why do you want this job?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I believe this job will build my confidence and improve my skills. I would love to grow with your company.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Why should we hire you?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Sir, I am a self-motivated person. As a fresher, I need a platform to use my knowledge. If you give me a chance, I will give my best for your company.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Why do you want to join us and not go for higher studies?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I believe this job will build my confidence and improve my skills. I would love to grow with your company. I am not leaving my studies. I will continue my studies along with work.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What do you know about our company?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Sir, your company is well known for customer service, and you also have a great relationship with your customers. Tip: Visit the company website the day before and replace this sample with real facts: what the company does, one service or client, and where the office is.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Are you willing to work night shifts or weekends?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: No, I do not have any problem with night shifts. Yes, I am willing to work on weekends. Tip: Answer in a full sentence and be honest. If you have a limit, say it politely before joining. Hindi: Poora sentence mein jawab do. Sach boliye.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Are you comfortable working in a team?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Yes, I am comfortable working in a team. I can also work independently without supervision. Tip: Add one short example from school, college or home.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Are you willing to work long hours if the project demands it?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Yes, I am willing to work long hours when the project demands it. Tip: Answer in a full sentence. Be honest about your limits.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Are you willing to relocate or travel?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I would definitely consider it. If the opportunity is appropriate, rewarding and feasible, I do not think I will have any issue with relocation or travel.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Where do you see yourself in 3 years? In 5 years?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: My current goal is to find a career position that ensures continued growth and new challenges every day. Three years from now, I see myself as an experienced and reliable senior member of the team. Five years from now, I expect to be ready for managerial responsibilities. I want a stable career in a single organisation, and I hope to get that wherever I start.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How long will you work for us after we hire you?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I am a fresher, and nothing is better for me than starting my professional career in a reputed company like yours. If everything goes well, I look forward to a long stay here, as long as the company needs me.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Do you have any questions for us?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Can I know about my role in detail? Tip: Never say "no". Ask about your role, the training or the shift timings.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How well do you handle change?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I try to stay focused on who I am and what I need. This helps me respond to change effectively. or (his longer answer): "Of course I can handle change. In my previous company, one of the bosses left. The new boss completely changed our strategy and project timings, and I was flexible and hard-working enough to manage it."

BPO / Call Centre.question: How quickly do you adapt to new technology?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I adapt quickly to new situations. I am clear about my job role and mentally prepared for challenges, so I can learn fast and apply my new knowledge. In my student life, I had to clear new papers and projects every semester and I enjoyed it. I will enjoy picking up new technologies in my professional life too.

BPO / Call Centre.question: How do you make important decisions?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I believe decisions should be made with all the information. If you miss an important detail, it is easy to make a bad decision. So I make important decisions after getting all the information.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Are you an organised person?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Yes, I am quite organised. I keep all my documents, certificates and files labelled and sorted, so I can find anything in seconds. I also keep my computer desktop clean.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Are you reliable? Can I trust you with responsibilities?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Yes, I am not only reliable but also very dependable. If a task is assigned to me, it will be handled properly and completed within the deadline.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What are the three most important things for you in a job?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Honesty, loyalty and determination to achieve my team's target. or "Professionalism, growth and a healthy work-life balance."

BPO / Call Centre.question: What motivates you?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: My biggest motivation is my family. They are my biggest source of inspiration and my strongest supporters. When I see my parents working, it gives me the drive to be like them. Their dedication motivates me.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What makes you happy?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Success makes me happy. I also feel happy after completing my tasks and achieving my goals. Holidays with my family also make me happy.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What makes you angry?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I get angry when I am falsely accused of something I did not do. Lack of order and discipline also irritates me, but I have learned to cope and adjust with other people.

BPO / Call Centre.question: If you could change one thing about your personality, what would it be?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I get easily frustrated with people who do not work hard. But I know people have different work styles and habits. So if I could change something, I would like to be more understanding.

BPO / Call Centre.question: Are you open to taking risks? Do you like experimenting?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: It is always good to venture into new areas and new technologies. I am an adaptive person and my diligence helps me pick up new things quickly. Taking risks can give good or bad results, but the exercise itself is a great learning experience. Such experiences create experts, and I want to become a subject matter expert (SME) someday.

BPO / Call Centre.question: On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate yourself as a leader?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: I rate my leadership skills 8 out of 10. There is much to learn, but I have always taken the lead. For example, [your example from school, college, sports, NCC or a group project]. Tip: Use one real example of leading a group. Do not copy someone else story.

BPO / Call Centre.question: If you won a Rs 10 crore lottery, would you still work?
BPO / Call Centre.hint: Sample answer: Yes, I would still work to build my career. With the lottery money, I will buy a big house for my mom and dad.

BPO / Call Centre.question: What is more important to you: money or success?

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Tell me about yourself in English.
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Name, city, studies, one strength (smile, teamwork, languages), why cabin crew. 5 sentences, clear voice, smile. Hindi: Naam, shehar, padhai, ek khoobi aur cabin crew kyun. Muskurakar saaf bolo.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Why do you want to be cabin crew?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Mention service to people, travel with responsibility, teamwork and safety. Avoid "I only want to travel and glamour". Hindi: Logon ki seva, safety, teamwork - sirf ghoomna ya glamour mat boliye.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Why do you want to join our airline?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Read about the airline: routes, base cities, service style, fleet. Say one thing you like. Hindi: Airline ke baare mein padho: routes, base city, service. Ek cheez jo pasand hai.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: What are the main duties of cabin crew?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Safety first (briefing, emergency, doors, seat belts), then service (welcome, meals, comfort), then handling passengers. Hindi: Pehle safety (briefing, emergency), phir service (swagat, khana), phir passengers ko sambhalna.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Which is more important for cabin crew: service or safety?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Safety. Cabin crew are first of all trained for safety; service comes next. Give a one-line reason. Hindi: Safety. Cabin crew sabse pehle safety ke liye hote hain.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Are you comfortable with height, weight and medical rules for this job?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Rules vary by airline (minimum height, weight in proportion, vision, no visible tattoos). Say you have read the rules and fit them. Be honest. Hindi: Rules airline ke hisaab se badalte hain (height, weight, aankhein). Padhkar sach batao.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: How is your reach? (Arm-reach test)
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Many airlines test if you can reach an overhead bin, often about 210 cm (varies). Say you will do the test and stretch fully. Hindi: Kai airline arm-reach test lete hain (overhead bin tak pahunch). Test mein poora stretch karo.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Are you comfortable with irregular shifts, nights and being away from home?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Say yes if true. Mention family support and that you will manage rest and health. Hindi: Raat ki shift, ghar se door rehna - sach boliye, family support batao.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Can you swim? Are you comfortable with heights and small spaces?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Some airlines ask. Answer honestly. If you cannot swim, say you will learn in training. Hindi: Kuch airline poochhte hain. Sach bolo, na aata ho to training mein seekhne ko bolo.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: A passenger is angry because the meal they ordered is finished. What will you do?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Apologise, stay calm, offer alternatives, ask a senior crew, thank them for understanding. Hindi: Sorry bolo, shaant raho, doosra option do, senior crew ko batao.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: A passenger refuses to fasten the seat belt or switch off the phone. What will you do?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Explain it is for their safety and the rules, ask politely twice, then call the senior crew. Do not argue. Hindi: Safety ka reason batao, politely 2 baar kaho, phir senior crew. Bahas nahi.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: A passenger feels sick or faints in flight. What will you do?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Stay calm, check, call senior crew and ask for a doctor on board, use first aid kit/oxygen as trained, tell the cockpit. Hindi: Shaant raho, senior crew ko batao, doctor ki announcement, first aid, cockpit ko batao.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: A child is crying and the parents are stressed. What do you do?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Speak kindly, offer water/toy/colouring if available, help the parents settle, stay patient. Hindi: Pyaar se baat, paani/khilona do, parents ko comfortable karo.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: What is IATA? Do you know any airport codes?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: IATA = International Air Transport Association. Three-letter airport codes: DEL (Delhi), BOM (Mumbai), BLR (Bengaluru), CCU (Kolkata), HYD (Hyderabad). Hindi: IATA airline ka international sangathan hai. DEL, BOM, BLR jaise 3-letter codes.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: How do you say the time in 24-hour format? What is 6 PM?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Airlines use the 24-hour clock. 6 PM = 1800 hours. Practise a few. Hindi: Airline mein 24-hour clock. Shaam 6 baje = 1800.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: What do you do during a safety demonstration?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Show seat belt, oxygen mask, life jacket and exits clearly while speaking, facing the passengers. Hindi: Seat belt, oxygen mask, life jacket, exits dikhana - passengers ki taraf dekhkar.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Tell me about a time you worked in a team.
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: A simple story from school, college, a function or home: your role, the work, the result. Hindi: School, college, ghar ka ek example: aapka role aur natija.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Strengths: polite, patient, team player. Small real weakness plus a fix. Keep it positive. Hindi: Strength: vinamra, patient. Chhoti kamzori aur sudhaar.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: How good is your English and Hindi? Do you know any other language?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Be honest. List the languages. Say you will practise daily. Hindi: Bhashaon ki list sach batao. Roz practise karne ki baat karo.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Can you stay calm in a stressful situation? Give an example.
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: A short story where you stayed calm (exam, a crowd, a family emergency). End with what you learned. Hindi: Exam ya emergency ka chhota example, aur seekh.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: What will you do if you are not selected this time?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Say you will ask for feedback, improve and apply again. Shows positive attitude. Hindi: Feedback loge, sudhaar karoge, phir apply karoge.

Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.question: Why should we hire you?
Cabin Crew / Air Hostess.hint: Three points: service attitude, calm in pressure, team player. Smile at the end. Hindi: Teen baatein: service ka bhav, pressure mein shaant, team player.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Tell me about yourself in English.
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Name, studies, city, hospitality course or skill if any, why hotels. Be polite and clean in appearance. Hindi: Naam, padhai, shehar, hospitality course/skill, hotel kyun. Vinamra raho.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Why do you want to work in the hotel industry?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Say you enjoy serving guests and learning. A good start for a long career. Not "only for tips or free food". Hindi: Guest ki seva aur seekhna pasand hai. Sirf tips/khane ke liye nahi.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What does "guest is God" (Atithi Devo Bhava) mean in a hotel?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Guests are treated with respect and care. Greet, listen, help quickly. Hindi: Guest ko izzat aur madad: swagat, suno, jaldi help.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What are the main departments in a hotel?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Front office, housekeeping, food and beverage service, kitchen, maintenance, security, sales. Hindi: Front office, housekeeping, F&B service, kitchen, maintenance, security.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What happens at guest check-in? And check-out?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Check-in: greet, ID proof, registration, room key, tell about breakfast and Wi-Fi. Check-out: bill, collect key, thank the guest, ask for feedback. Hindi: Check-in: swagat, ID, form, chaabi, facilities. Check-out: bill, chaabi, dhanyawad, feedback.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What is the usual check-in and check-out time?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Many hotels use 12 or 2 PM for check-in and 11 AM or 12 noon for check-out (varies by hotel). Say you would follow the hotel policy. Hindi: Hotel ke hisaab se badalta hai - policy follow karo.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: A guest arrives early and the room is not ready. What do you do?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Apologise, offer to keep luggage, a seat in the lobby, a welcome drink, and update them when the room is ready. Hindi: Sorry, saaman rakhwao, lobby mein baithao, drink do, room ready hote hi batao.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: A guest complains that the room is not clean. What will you do?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Listen, apologise, note the room number, send housekeeping fast or change the room, follow up after. Hindi: Suno, sorry, room number note, housekeeping bhejo ya room badlo, baad mein poochho.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: The guest says the food is cold. What will you do?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Apologise, take the dish back, tell the kitchen, serve a fresh dish, check again with the guest. Hindi: Sorry, dish wapas, kitchen ko batao, naya serve, guest se confirm.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: A guest asks for something that is against hotel policy. What do you say?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Say no politely, explain the rule, offer an alternative, and ask a senior if needed. Hindi: Politely na, rule samjhao, alternative do, senior se poochho.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What is "upselling"? Give an example.
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Offering a better room, a meal combo or a service so the guest enjoys more. Example: "Would you like a sea-view room for a little extra?" Hindi: Guest ko behtar room ya service suggest karna. Example: "Sea-view room lena chahenge?"

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Two guests want the last available room. What will you do?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Check booking priority, be fair and honest, offer another hotel or date if needed, tell your manager. Hindi: Booking dekho, imaandaari se, alternative, manager ko batao.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: How do you answer a hotel phone call?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: "Good morning, Hotel [name], [your name] speaking, how may I help you?" Smile, speak slowly, note the message. Hindi: "Good morning, Hotel [naam], main [aapka naam], kya madad kar sakta/sakti hoon?"

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Are you comfortable with rotational shifts, night duty and festival work?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Hotels never close. Say yes if true and mention your family's support. Hindi: Hotel 24x7 chalte hain. Shift, raat aur tyohar - sach boliye.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Can you stand for long hours? Are you comfortable with a uniform and grooming rules?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Yes. Say you keep neat hair, clean nails, proper uniform, and good hygiene. Hindi: Haan. Safai, uniform, grooming ka dhyan.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: How do you handle guest information and security?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Keep it private. Never share room numbers or names with strangers. Check ID. Hindi: Guest ki jaankari private. Kisi ko room number mat batao. ID check.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What do you do if you see something suspicious or lost property?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Do not touch. Tell the supervisor or security. Record the place and time. Lost property goes to the lost-and-found desk. Hindi: Haath mat lagao, supervisor/security ko batao, jagah aur time note.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Tell me about a time you worked in a team.
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: A short story from school, college, a family function or a part-time job. Hindi: Chhoti kahani: aapka kaam, natija.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Strength: polite, hard-working. A small, honest weakness and how you fix it. Hindi: Ek strength, ek chhoti kamzori aur fix.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: What salary do you expect?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: As a fresher, follow hotel standards. Say you want training and growth. Ask about meals, uniform and accommodation. Hindi: Fresher ke hisaab se. Training aur growth pe zor. Meal, uniform, rehne ki jagah poochho.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Where do you see yourself in 3 years?
Hotel & Hospitality.hint: Supervisor or senior executive, after learning the work well. Hindi: Supervisor ya senior executive.

Hotel & Hospitality.question: Why should we hire you?

Airport Ground Staff.question: What does ground staff do?

Airport Ground Staff.question: What documents does a passenger need for a domestic flight? For an international flight?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Domestic: valid photo ID and ticket. International: passport and visa if needed, ticket. Tell the check-in rule from your airline. Hindi: Domestic: ID aur ticket. International: passport, visa, ticket.

Airport Ground Staff.question: What happens at check-in?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Greet, check ID and ticket, weigh the bags, tag them, give the boarding pass with seat and gate, tell the boarding time. Hindi: Swagat, ID/ticket, bag weight, tag, boarding pass, time batao.

Airport Ground Staff.question: What is the baggage allowance? What if a bag is overweight?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: It varies by airline and ticket. Typical domestic cabin bag is about 7 kg (varies). If the checked bag is overweight, tell the passenger the excess-baggage fee or ask them to remove items. Hindi: Airline ke hisaab se. Overweight ho to excess fee ya saaman kam karao.

Airport Ground Staff.question: What items are not allowed in a cabin bag?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Sharp objects, lighters, flammable liquids, power banks in checked bag (rules apply), large liquids. Say "as per the security rule". Hindi: Tez cheezein, lighter, jwalansheel cheezein, bade liquid. Security rule ke hisaab se.

Airport Ground Staff.question: When does check-in close and when does boarding close?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: It varies by airline and airport. Domestic check-in usually closes around 45-60 minutes before departure. Say you would follow the airline's rule. Hindi: Airline par depend. Domestic check-in aam taur par 45-60 min pehle band hota hai.

Airport Ground Staff.question: A passenger arrives late after check-in closed. What will you do?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Stay polite, explain the rule, check with the supervisor if any option exists, help them rebook. Hindi: Politely rule batao, supervisor se poochho, rebook mein madad.

Airport Ground Staff.question: A flight is delayed by two hours and passengers are angry. What do you do?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Announce the truth and expected time, apologise, offer water/snacks as the airline allows, update every 15-30 minutes. Hindi: Sahi jaankari, sorry, paani/snacks (rule se), baar baar update.

Airport Ground Staff.question: A passenger's bag did not arrive. What will you do?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Apologise, take them to the baggage service desk, fill the lost-baggage report (PIR), give the reference number. Hindi: Sorry, baggage desk par le jao, report bharo, reference number do.

Airport Ground Staff.question: A passenger with a wheelchair or an elderly person needs help. What do you do?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Ask kindly, arrange the wheelchair, tell the staff, walk with them to the gate, thank them. Hindi: Pyaar se poochho, wheelchair arrange, gate tak saath.

Airport Ground Staff.question: A passenger insists on a window seat that is already taken. What will you do?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Explain, check the seat map, offer the nearest option or ask another passenger kindly, never argue. Hindi: Samjhao, seat map dekho, nazdeeki option, bahas nahi.

Airport Ground Staff.question: You see an unattended bag at the gate. What do you do?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Do not touch. Ask nearby people if it is theirs, move people away, inform security and your supervisor at once. Hindi: Haath mat lagao, aas-paas poochho, security aur supervisor ko turant batao.

Airport Ground Staff.question: What do you do if a passenger is on the no-fly or security-flagged list?
Airport Ground Staff.hint: Do not argue. Follow the procedure and call security or the supervisor. Keep the passenger's information private. Hindi: Bahas nahi. Procedure, security/supervisor, jaankari private.
